config.title: Context Performance

intro.title: Context Performance
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple React app that demonstrates how to optimize performance when using the Context API. You'll learn to prevent unnecessary re-renders by splitting context providers and using React.memo. The core concept is understanding how context updates trigger component re-renders and applying techniques to control them. You'll work with React hooks like useContext, useState, and the React.memo higher-order component. By the end, you'll have a functional app that efficiently updates only the relevant parts of the UI when context values change.
intro.usecase: In complex React applications like e-commerce platforms or analytics dashboards, context performance optimization is crucial when multiple components depend on shared state. For example, a product filtering system where dozens of UI elements (price sliders, category checkboxes, sort dropdowns) all consume filter state from a single context. Without proper optimization, changing one filter could trigger unnecessary re-renders across the entire interface, causing laggy user interactions. Developers implement context performance patterns to ensure that only the relevant components update when context values change, maintaining smooth UX in data-heavy applications.

objectives: Initialize a React context with default values
Configure a context provider to wrap application components
Apply the useContext hook to access context values in child components
Manipulate context values through provider state updates
Construct a performance-optimized context by preventing unnecessary re-renders
Integrate memoization techniques to control component updates within context
Render components that selectively respond to specific context value changes

steps.title: Import React, useState, useContext, createContext and useMemo
steps.instruction: Import React, useState, useContext, createContext, and useMemo from 'react'.
steps.hint: Use a single import statement with curly braces to import multiple named exports from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple hooks from React
import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and the required hooks here
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary React APIs and hooks are imported, enabling you to use state, context, and memoization in this lesson.
successCriteria: React, useState, useContext, createContext, and useMemo are all imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've imported all the required React hooks and APIs. This gives you the foundation to work with state, context, and performance optimizations.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some of the required items, but not all. Make sure to import React, useState, useContext, createContext, and useMemo from 'react' in a single import statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import React, useState, useContext, createContext, and useMemo from 'react' to proceed with this lesson.

steps.title: Create a ThemeContext using createContext
steps.instruction: Create a ThemeContext using React.createContext() and export it.
steps.hint: Use createContext to create a new context object. Remember to export it so it can be imported in other files.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ThemeContext object is created and exported, ready to hold theme values.
successCriteria: ThemeContext is created with createContext and exported.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a ThemeContext using createContext. This context will serve as the container for your theme values throughout the app.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're both creating the context with createContext() and exporting it so other components can use it.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create a ThemeContext using React.createContext() and export it so it can be imported elsewhere.

steps.title: Create a ThemeProvider component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ThemeProvider that accepts children as props.
steps.hint: Define a component that takes children as a parameter and returns them wrapped in ThemeContext.Provider.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ThemeProvider component is defined that can wrap children.
successCriteria: ThemeProvider is a functional component that accepts children as props.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the ThemeProvider component that will manage theme state for the app.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure ThemeProvider is a functional component that accepts children as a prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: ThemeProvider should be a functional component that accepts children as props. Check the syntax.

steps.title: Initialize theme state in ThemeProvider
steps.instruction: Inside the ThemeProvider component, use useState to create a state variable called 'theme' initialized to the string 'light'.
steps.hint: Call useState with the initial value 'light' and destructure the returned array into two variables: theme and setTheme.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ThemeProvider component should have a 'theme' state variable initialized to 'light'.
successCriteria: ThemeProvider uses useState to declare a 'theme' state variable initialized to 'light'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the theme state with useState.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState to create a state variable called 'theme' with initial value 'light'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to use useState inside ThemeProvider to create a 'theme' state variable initialized to 'light'.

steps.title: Create toggleTheme handler in ThemeProvider
steps.instruction: Inside the ThemeProvider component, create a function named toggleTheme that toggles the theme state between 'light' and 'dark'.
steps.hint: The function should update the theme state using the setTheme function. Use the previous state to determine the new theme value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A toggleTheme function is defined inside ThemeProvider that toggles the theme state between 'light' and 'dark'.
successCriteria: The toggleTheme function is created and correctly toggles the theme state value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the toggleTheme handler that will switch between light and dark themes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it properly toggles between 'light' and 'dark' using the setTheme function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleTheme function is missing or doesn't correctly toggle the theme state. Review how to update state based on previous state.

steps.title: Memoize context value with useMemo
steps.instruction: Inside the ThemeProvider component, use the useMemo hook to create a memoized context value object containing theme and toggleTheme.
steps.hint: Call useMemo with a function that returns an object with theme and toggleTheme properties, and pass [theme] as the dependency array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ThemeProvider component now includes a useMemo call that creates a memoized object with theme and toggleTheme properties.
successCriteria: useMemo is called with a function returning { theme, toggleTheme } and [theme] as dependency array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully memoized the context value object to prevent unnecessary re-renders.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure useMemo returns an object with both theme and toggleTheme properties, and includes [theme] as the dependency array.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Use useMemo to create a memoized object containing theme and toggleTheme, with theme as the dependency.

steps.title: Return ThemeContext.Provider with memoized value
steps.instruction: In the ThemeProvider component, update the ThemeContext.Provider's value prop to use the memoized context value you created in the previous step.
steps.hint: The value prop should receive the memoized object containing theme and toggleTheme.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ThemeContext.Provider now provides the memoized context value to its children.
successCriteria: ThemeContext.Provider's value prop is set to the memoizedValue variable.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully provided the memoized context value to the ThemeContext.Provider. This ensures child components receive a stable reference when theme doesn't change.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're passing the memoizedValue variable to the value prop of ThemeContext.Provider.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ThemeContext.Provider should receive the memoizedValue as its value prop. Check that you're using the correct variable name.

steps.title: Create a ThemedButton component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ThemedButton that uses useContext to access the ThemeContext and returns a button element.
steps.hint: Use the useContext hook with ThemeContext to get the context value, then return a <button> element.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ThemedButton component is created that will later be used to display a theme-aware button.
successCriteria: ThemedButton component is defined, uses useContext with ThemeContext, and returns a button element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the ThemedButton component that will consume the theme context.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a component, but make sure it uses useContext with ThemeContext and returns a button element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't properly defined yet. Create a functional component named ThemedButton that uses useContext to access ThemeContext and returns a button.

steps.title: Add button styling based on theme
steps.instruction: Inside the ThemedButton component, add conditional styling to the button element so it has a dark background when the theme is 'dark' and a light background when the theme is 'light'.
steps.hint: You can use a ternary operator to set the button's style attribute conditionally based on the theme value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The button should have different background colors based on the current theme value from context.
successCriteria: The button element has a style attribute with conditional backgroundColor based on the theme value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional styling to the button based on the theme context value.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're applying the style attribute to the button and using the theme value to conditionally set the backgroundColor.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button doesn't have conditional styling based on the theme. Check that you're using the theme value from context and applying it to the button's style attribute.

steps.title: Wire onClick to toggleTheme handler
steps.instruction: In the ThemedButton component, add an onClick handler to the button that calls the toggleTheme function from context.
steps.hint: Use the toggleTheme function from the context object you already destructured.
steps.expectedOutcome: The button will have an onClick handler that triggers the theme toggle functionality when clicked.
successCriteria: The button element has an onClick attribute that calls toggleTheme from the context.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wired the button click to the toggleTheme handler. This connects the UI interaction with the context state update.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling toggleTheme from the context object. Remember you can destructure it alongside theme.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button still needs an onClick handler. Try adding onClick={toggleTheme} to the button element after getting toggleTheme from the context.

steps.title: Create main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns a div containing the ThemeProvider and ThemedButton components.
steps.hint: Define the App component above the export statement, then return the ThemeProvider wrapping the ThemedButton inside a div.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns a div containing ThemeProvider and ThemedButton.
successCriteria: App component is defined and returns a div with ThemeProvider wrapping ThemedButton.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the main App component that structures the application with the ThemeProvider and ThemedButton.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the App component, but make sure it returns a div containing ThemeProvider with ThemedButton as its child.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component is not properly defined. Create a functional component named App that returns a div with ThemeProvider wrapping ThemedButton.

steps.title: Wrap app with ThemeProvider and add ThemedButton
steps.instruction: In the App component, return the ThemeProvider wrapping the ThemedButton component.
steps.hint: The ThemeProvider should be the outermost element, with ThemedButton as its child.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component renders the ThemeProvider with ThemedButton as its child, completing the context setup.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully wrapped the app with ThemeProvider and added ThemedButton, completing the context performance example.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the App component returns the ThemeProvider with ThemedButton as its child.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component should return ThemeProvider wrapping ThemedButton. Check the structure of your return statement.
